title: A Rectifier-Less Piezoelectric Energy-Harvesting Interface with a Sense & Track MPPT Achieving Single-Cycle Convergence and 568% Shock Power Improvement
problem: Existing piezoelectric energy harvesting (PEH) systems with bias-flip rectifiers and MPPT perform well under periodic vibrations but degrade sharply under shock conditions due to slow impedance-matching speed for fast amplitude variations.
motivation: Edge IoT sensors need efficient energy harvesting from real-world environments with both periodical vibrations and shocks; battery-powered IoT cannot scale to billions of edge devices.
method: The system removes the traditional rectifier that converts piezoelectric vibrations into electrical power, eliminating the energy wasted in that conversion step. Instead, it uses a sense-and-track algorithm that continuously measures the vibration and adjusts the electrical impedance (the load resistance) in analog electronics to match the current vibration amplitude. This adjustment completes in a single vibration cycle—fast enough to keep up with sudden shock impacts where the amplitude changes rapidly. By skipping the rectifier and adapting this quickly, it extracts more power than traditional systems, especially under shock conditions.
key_novelty: Single-cycle maximum power point convergence using a rectifier-free design and sense-and-track algorithm allows instant adaptation to fast-changing shock vibrations.
contributions: 568% shock power improvement over conventional MPPT
Single-cycle MPP convergence enabling real-time adaptation
Unified handling of periodical vibrations and shock excitations
primary_theme: Fast-adaptive piezoelectric energy harvesting for edge IoT
